table.title: EN · Plan comparison
table.md:
| Feature | Free | Pro | Enterprise | Notes |
|---|:-:|:-:|:-:|---|
| Projects | 3 | Unlimited | Unlimited | Archived projects do not count toward the limit. |
| Storage | 2 GB | 100 GB | Custom | Additional storage can be purchased in 50 GB blocks. |
| SSO / SAML | — | — | ✓ | Supports Okta, Azure AD and any SAML 2.0 identity provider. |
| Audit log | — | 30 days | 1 year | |
| Support | Community | Email | 24/7 phone & dedicated manager | Response time targets are defined in the SLA. |

understanding.purpose: Compare Free, Pro, and Enterprise plan capabilities feature by feature, with Notes supplying caveats and context.
understanding.reading: Readers scan down the Feature labels, then compare across the three plan columns; Notes is read afterward as supporting detail.
groups: Free, Pro, and Enterprise belong together as parallel plan-value columns and should remain easy to compare.
Feature is the row-label column and anchors each comparison.
Notes is a separate explanatory column and should not compete with the plan values.
keep_intact: Headers: Feature, Free, Pro, Enterprise, Notes
Short plan values such as Unlimited, Community, 30 days, 1 year, and Custom
Tokens such as SSO / SAML and 24/7
Numeric units such as 2 GB and 100 GB
may_wrap: The long Enterprise support phrase at word boundaries

preferred.name: r2C
preferred.note: A middle setting between the two above: Notes at 193 (172px text) clears the 3-line threshold with margin instead of sitting on the boundary, and Enterprise at 132 (111px text) stays comfortably wider than "Unlimited" so the plan trio reads evenly rather than one column looking squeezed. Safer against font/rendering variance than notes-3line while still removing the extra Notes line that inflated r1A/r1B.

acceptable.name: r2A
acceptable.note: Trim Feature to its true minimum (114 = 93px label + 21), Free to 109 ("Community" = 88px) and Pro to 94 ("Unlimited"), then hand the recovered ~20px to Notes. Notes now has 165px of text, enough for the SSO note to break into 3 lines instead of 4, while Enterprise keeps 118px — enough for the "Enterprise" header (83px), "Unlimited" (88px) and a 3-line word-boundary wrap of the support phrase.

acceptable.name: r2B
acceptable.note: Push the same trade to its limit: Enterprise sits at 120px, the smallest width that still keeps "Unlimited" and the "Enterprise" header intact on one line, and Notes takes 205px (184px of text). This drops the Projects and Support notes to 2 lines and holds the rest at 3, so the prose column stops dictating tall rows; the cost is a compact, slightly tight Enterprise column, acceptable because its values are short and parallel to Free/Pro.

acceptable.name: r1A
acceptable.note: Trim the over-wide Feature column from 150px to 115px and tighten Pro to 95px, then give the recovered space to Enterprise (151px). Feature, Free and Pro now fit their one-line content; Enterprise avoids the lone “&” break, and Notes keeps 150px of content for its explanatory prose.

acceptable.name: r1B
acceptable.note: Refine the compact r0B layout: widen Feature from 104px to 114px so SSO / SAML fits, and widen Enterprise from 116px to 145px so its support phrase is less fragmented. Fund this by reducing Notes from 209px to 178px and tightening Free and Pro, preserving Notes readability while restoring the plan columns.

acceptable.name: r1C
acceptable.note: Prioritize the plan comparison: give Enterprise 168px so the support phrase can break cleanly into two lines, while keeping Feature, Free and Pro safely above their no-wrap thresholds. Notes becomes narrower at 154px and will wrap more, but the three plan values gain visual authority and the comparison scans better.

bad.name: r3A
bad.note: Take 7px from Notes and give them to Enterprise versus r2A (139/186 → 146/180). Enterprise text grows to 125px, giving the "24/7 phone &" break about 23px of margin instead of 16px, so it cannot fall into r2B's leading-ampersand break. Notes stays at 180px (159px text), still wide enough to keep "50 GB blocks." intact and every note at three lines, so no row grows.
bad.why: Free and Pro are each 1px too narrow, so 'Community' splits as 'Communit y' and 'Unlimited' splits as 'Unlimite d'. Mid-word splits destroy scanability and make the table look broken.

bad.name: r3B
bad.note: Test the unexplored trade: push Enterprise to 166px (145px text) so the support phrase breaks into two balanced lines, "24/7 phone &" / "dedicated manager", eliminating the orphan. Notes drops to 160px (139px text); notes remain three lines but with less slack, so the Projects note is the one at risk of a fourth line. Worth noting this buys no height — the Support row stays 92px either way because its Notes cell is three lines — so it is a purely typographic gain paid for in Notes tightness.
bad.why: Same mid-word splits as r3A, plus a taller 501px table caused by starving the Notes column; it combines broken identifiers with inefficient height.

rationale: r2C is the cleanest balance: it keeps the three plan columns just wide enough for their longest values, then gives the remaining width to Notes, so the table stays 448px tall with no mid-word splits and only the prose cells wrapping. r2A leaves Notes too narrow, pushing the support note to three lines, while r2B overcorrects and breaks Enterprise as '24/7 phone' / '& dedicated' / 'manager', starting a line with an ampersand. The r1 designs are readable but spend height on four-line note cells; r1C in particular makes the prose column too narrow. r3A and r3B are unacceptable because Free and Pro fall just below the content width needed to keep 'Community' and 'Unlimited' intact.

general: Size short value columns to the longest unbreakable token plus padding; a 1px shortfall can force mid-word splits, which readers notice immediately.
Prose columns should absorb leftover width; equal widths waste space in short numeric columns and starve explanatory notes.
Headers are often narrower than data cells, so size columns by the data that must stay intact, not by the header label.
Overall row height is set by the tallest cell; rebalancing widths can remove a line from one column without adding one to another.
Avoid line breaks that strand conjunctions or ampersands at the start of a line in narrow value cells.
specific: Feature needs about 114px to keep 'SSO / SAML' on one line; Free needs at least 109px for 'Community'; Pro needs at least 94px for 'Unlimited'.
Enterprise at roughly 132–145px keeps the support value in acceptable lines, while Notes at roughly 190–205px keeps the support note to two lines and the SSO note to three.
This table's Notes column carries full explanatory sentences, so it should be the widest column rather than Enterprise.
The 448px r2 family is the shortest safe height; r1's 474–527px height comes from under-allocating Notes.

tradeoffs: A designer could prefer r2A's wider Enterprise column and accept a three-line support note, or choose r2B's wider Notes column despite the awkward leading ampersand in Enterprise. The exact point where a cell drops from three lines to two depends on font rendering, so a few pixels of disagreement is reasonable.
uncertain: Whether 'SSO / SAML' can wrap without looking broken, whether a leading '&' is a publishable break, and whether r1C's taller but still intact layout is acceptable for a dense reference table.

critique.good: All headers stay on one line, no mid-word splits, and the plan values are generally readable. The Feature column anchors rows clearly.
critique.problems: SSO / SAML wraps onto two lines, adding avoidable height. Notes prose is cramped: SSO and Support run to four lines. The table is tall at 501px with uneven row heights.
critique.cause: Feature is 112px, leaving 91px of content, 2px short of the 93px needed for SSO / SAML. Notes is 163px (142px content), too narrow for its prose. Enterprise at 150px leaves 129px, so the support phrase takes three lines. Free is also over-wide relative to Pro.

critique.good: Shortest table at 422px, Notes prose reads comfortably, headers stay intact, and there are no mid-word splits.
critique.problems: SSO / SAML wraps, and the Enterprise support value breaks into awkward fragments, including a line beginning with “& dedicated” and an orphaned “manager.” The plan columns look cramped beside the very wide Notes column, weakening comparison.
critique.cause: Feature is 104px, giving only 83px against the 93px needed. Enterprise is 116px, giving 95px, far below the roughly 147px needed for a clean two-line support phrase. Notes at 209px is over-allocated, taking space from the plan columns.

critique.good: Feature and all headers stay on one line, no mid-word splits, and Free/Pro values are clean. The row labels read as clear anchors.
critique.problems: Feature is visibly over-wide, creating dead space. Enterprise is severely cramped: the support phrase runs to four lines with a lone “&” line, forcing a 118px row. Notes still runs to four lines for SSO, and the table remains 501px tall.
critique.cause: Feature at 150px leaves 129px when 93px suffices, wasting about 36px. Enterprise at 110px leaves only 89px, causing the extreme wrapping. That wasted Feature width should go to Enterprise and Notes.

critique.good: Plan trio reads comfortably and stays parallel: Free 110 fits "Community" (88px) on one line, Pro 95 fits "Unlimited", all five headers sit on one line, and the 3-line Support phrase breaks cleanly at word boundaries. Feature at 115 is correctly minimal for the widest label (93px + 21px padding).
critique.problems: Rows 1–3 and 5 are 92–118px tall with a single token floating at the top of Free/Pro/Enterprise, leaving big dead boxes under the plan values; the Notes column looks like the cramped afterthought even though it is the only column that carries prose. The SSO note runs to 4 lines and the other notes to 3, which is what sets every row height.
critique.cause: Notes gets only 171px (150px of text) while Enterprise holds 151px for a support phrase that will never fit on one line anyway (it needs 255px+). Roughly 15–20px transferred from Enterprise to Notes would drop the SSO note to 3 lines and shorten three rows.

critique.good: Slightly more room for Notes and still no mid-word splits; headers all on one line; the Enterprise checkmark and short values stay legible.
critique.problems: Visually almost indistinguishable from r1A: the Support cell still wraps to 3 lines, the SSO note still takes 4 lines, and row heights are identical (92/92/118/39/92). Meanwhile Enterprise has become the narrowest of the three plan columns while Free (110) and Pro (95) kept their width, so the plan trio's rhythm is now uneven.
critique.cause: A 7px transfer (Enterprise 145, Notes 178) is below the line-break threshold — the SSO note needs about +15px of text width to lose a line, so nothing changed except the Enterprise column's proportion.

critique.good: Enterprise now has real breathing room for "24/7 phone & dedicated manager" and the plan columns look evenly weighted; headers still unwrapped.
critique.problems: The table grew to 527px: Storage, SSO and Support rows are all 118px (4 lines) with wide empty bands beside them in Free/Pro, and Notes is visibly the tightest column in the table, breaking "Additional / storage can be / purchased in 50 / GB blocks." The Enterprise cell it was paid for still shows the Support phrase on 3 lines, so the extra width bought nothing.
critique.cause: 17px were moved into Enterprise (151→168) which does not remove a line (the phrase needs ~276px to sit on one line), and those 17px were taken from Notes (171→154 = 133px of text), crossing the break threshold the wrong way and adding a 4th line to three notes — the only place where a lost pixel costs 26px of row height.

critique.good: Closest to the working window: Enterprise 139px (text 118px) is just wide enough to break as "24/7 phone &" / "dedicated" / "manager", so no line starts with an ampersand; Notes 186px (165px text) keeps "50 GB blocks." together and holds every note to three lines, matching the 92px row rhythm. Feature/Free/Pro sit exactly at their no-wrap minimums (114/109/94), so no width is wasted there.
critique.problems: The Support cell ends on an orphan line containing only "manager". The Enterprise break has almost no safety margin, and the Notes column is the narrowest of the three designs without gaining anything in line count.
critique.cause: Enterprise 139px puts "24/7 phone &" (about 102px) on line 1 but "dedicated manager" (about 145px) cannot fit 118px, so "manager" drops alone. Notes 186px is already enough for three-line notes, so the 19px r2A keeps out of Notes buys nothing.

critique.good: Notes 205px (184px text) is the most comfortable prose column: lines are full, "50 GB" stays intact, and the Notes text no longer looks cramped.
critique.problems: The Enterprise column is visibly squeezed next to Free/Pro and the Support phrase breaks badly: "24/7 phone" / "& dedicated" / "manager" — a line beginning with an ampersand plus an orphan. It is the weakest read of the three and undercuts Enterprise as the premium column.
critique.cause: Enterprise 120px leaves only 99px of text, which is below the ~102px needed for "24/7 phone &", so the ampersand is pushed to the start of line 2; the 19px taken from Enterprise is pure over-allocation to Notes, which was already at three lines.

critique.good: Enterprise 132px (111px text) still avoids the leading-ampersand break, and the overall column rhythm is even.
critique.problems: Notes 193px (172px text) produces the worst break of the three: "Additional storage can be / purchased in 50 / GB blocks." — the numeric unit "50 GB" is split across lines. Widening Notes actually degraded it.
critique.cause: At 172px, "purchased in 50" fills the line and "GB" no longer fits, so the unit is severed; the fill point sits just past the safe threshold that 165px (r2A) and 184px (r2B) both clear.

review.method: two fresh-context blind reviews; letters shuffled; includes browser auto layout and equal widths as neutral references

r3A.why: Words break mid-token — "Unlimite d" in Pro and "Communit y" in Free — because those columns were sized below their longest unbreakable word; the table reads as damaged text.

r2A.why: Feature labels stay on one line, Free/Pro/Enterprise are compact but never break a word, and Notes gets ~190px so the prose reads in three clean lines; column rhythm tracks content.

ref_equal.why: Notes is starved to ~110px, stacking the prose into 5–7 ragged lines, while Free/Pro/Enterprise sit on wide near-empty fields — effort is spent on the columns that need it least.

ref_auto.why: Overall balanced and no word is broken, but the first column is too narrow: "SSO / SAML" wraps to two lines, so row labels stop reading as consistent single-line units.

r2C.why: Effectively B with a slightly wider Notes; plan columns stay tight, all words and labels intact, and the prose column carries its weight without stealing from the numbers.

r2B.why: Sound and unbroken, but Enterprise is trimmed enough that "24/7 phone & dedicated manager" breaks into three short lines while Notes gains slack it does not need — a mild inversion of emphasis.

raw.unsure: B and E are nearly identical at this resolution (only a few px of Notes/Enterprise differ), so I cannot reliably separate them; D's narrow label column may be a deliberate row-label treatment rather than an error.

ref_equal.why: All words stay intact, but Notes is starved into 5–7 lines while Free and Pro carry excess width, making rows unnecessarily tall and uneven.

r2A.why: Clean and readable: headers and values stay intact, Notes wraps to 3–4 lines, and column proportions are sensible, though Notes is slightly tighter than in D.

r3A.why: Pro is too narrow, breaking “Unlimited” into “Unlimite d,” and Free breaks “Community”; mid-word breaks make the table look broken.

r2C.why: Balanced and publication-ready: Feature and all headers fit comfortably, no words break, and Notes has enough width to stay compact in 3 lines.

r2B.why: Very close to D: no broken words and compact Notes, but the Enterprise header is squeezed with almost no side breathing room.

ref_auto.why: Notes is generously wide, but Feature is squeezed so “SSO / SAML” wraps and the Feature header is tight; the extra Notes width does not reduce line count.

raw.unsure: Pixel widths are inferred from the screenshots; D and E are very close, and reasonable viewers might prefer E's wider Notes despite its tighter Enterprise header.

provenance.note: AI visual design judgement; not a human reading study
